privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.summary: How personal data is handled on the Situate website, in the Situate app and when you contact us.
privacy.scope.title: What this notice covers
privacy.scope.body: This notice covers getsituate.com, the preview at reboot.getsituate.com, the platform waitlist, direct downloads and updates, and enquiries by email or telephone. The app sections cover the macOS and iOS builds of Situate distributed or linked through this website or Apple. Availability depends on the platform and release channel. Processing by connected providers, Apple and services you choose is also subject to their own privacy information.
privacy.controller.title: Who is responsible
privacy.controller.body: For the website, waitlist, release delivery and contact processing we operate, the controller is:
privacy.hosting.title: Visiting the website
privacy.hosting.provider: The website and direct macOS release files are served from our self-managed server at Hetzner in Nuremberg, Germany. The infrastructure provider is Hetzner Online GmbH, Industriestr. 25, 91710 Gunzenhausen, Germany.
privacy.hosting.data: When you request a page or a file, the server processes your IP address, the date and time, the requested address, the response status and technical request information, such as your browser's user agent. This information is needed to establish the connection and deliver the requested content.
privacy.hosting.purpose: We process this information to provide the website, resolve technical faults and protect the service against misuse. The legal basis is our legitimate interest in operating a secure, reliable website under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.
privacy.hosting.logs: The static web server disables access logs and records errors at warning level and above. Operational logs can contain technical request information. Container logs for the production website, preview website and shared reverse proxy rotate at three files of 10 MiB per container, replacing older files as new output is written. This is a size limit, not a fixed retention period. These limits do not govern host security logs or Hetzner's own infrastructure records.
privacy.hosting.securityLogs: The host also keeps system and security logs. Authentication logs use weekly rotation with up to four rotated files; empty files are not rotated, and older rotated files are compressed. This rotation schedule does not guarantee deletion after a fixed number of days. System journal retention is separate from these file and container rotation limits.
privacy.browser.title: Cookies, browser storage and external content
privacy.browser.storage: Your browser may cache website files. If analytics is configured, the website remembers your analytics choice in browser storage. Analytics identifiers are stored only with your consent, as described below. Opening the optional sign-up form loads third-party services, which may use cookies or browser storage under their own policies.
privacy.browser.analytics: We use PostHog on getsituate.com only after you allow analytics. If you allow it, we measure page visits, download clicks, opening the waitlist form and successful form responses. The legal basis is your consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR and, for storing or accessing non-essential browser information, Section 25(1) TDDDG. Declining does not restrict the website, downloads or waitlist. We do not use advertising trackers, session recording or third-party video players. The optional waitlist form loads EmailOctopus and Google services only after you choose to open it.
privacy.browser.analyticsData: Analytics events contain a random browser identifier and session identifier, the page path without query parameters or fragments, the referring hostname, a coarse device category and, for download clicks, the advertised app version. These identifiers are pseudonymous, not anonymous people. We do not send email addresses, form contents or application identifiers. IP-derived location is disabled; PostHog still receives connection information when your browser contacts it.
privacy.browser.analyticsStorage: We remember your analytics choice in local browser storage for 180 days. If you allow analytics, the website also stores a PostHog-generated browser identifier in local storage. Session identifiers and other SDK state remain in page memory, not browser storage. Use Analytics preferences in the footer to withdraw consent. This stops further collection and clears the website's analytics identifiers where browser storage is accessible. Requests already sent and data already stored by PostHog are not undone by withdrawal. An expired choice is checked when you return and while the page is open.
privacy.browser.analyticsProvider: Analytics uses PostHog Cloud EU, operated by PostHog, Inc. (United States), as our processor under a data processing agreement. Hosting in the EU does not exclude processing outside the European Economic Area, including in the United States. The agreement incorporates the European Commission's EU Standard Contractual Clauses (Module 2) for transfers to PostHog. PostHog publishes its subprocessors and their processing locations in the list linked below.
privacy.browser.analyticsRetention: The analytics project retains events for one year. PostHog deletes events older than this window at its next monthly cleanup, rather than exactly when an event turns one year old. Contact us to request deletion of your analytics data.
credits.posthog: The website includes the PostHog JavaScript SDK, version 1.447.4, under its Apache-2.0 and MIT license terms, including third-party notices.
credits.posthogLicense: PostHog SDK license and third-party notices
privacy.browser.links: Following an external link takes you to a different website, whose operator processes your request under its own privacy notice. An email link opens your email application; it does not submit a message through this website.
privacy.waitlist.title: Platform updates and beta invitations
privacy.waitlist.purpose: If you join the waitlist, we use your email address and selected platforms to send availability updates for Situate. If you separately opt in to beta testing, we may also contact you with beta invitations. Joining does not subscribe you to a general marketing newsletter. The legal basis for these emails is your consent under Article 6(1)(a) GDPR.
privacy.waitlist.providers: We use EmailOctopus (Three Hearts Digital Ltd, 86-90 Paul Street, Shoreditch, London EC2A 4NE, United Kingdom) to manage subscriptions and send these emails. Opening the form connects your browser to EmailOctopus and Google for sign-up, reCAPTCHA spam protection and form fonts. These services receive technical request information, including your IP address and browser information. Submitting sends your email address, platform choices and optional beta preference to EmailOctopus.
privacy.waitlist.confirmation: We ask new subscribers to confirm their email address before receiving updates. You can withdraw consent at any time using the unsubscribe link in our emails or by contacting us. Withdrawal does not affect the lawfulness of processing before withdrawal. Contact us to change your platform choices or beta preference.
privacy.waitlist.retention: We keep subscription information while you remain subscribed and the platform update list is in use. After withdrawal, we retain only information needed to respect your opt-out and document consent where legally necessary.
privacy.waitlist.transfers: EmailOctopus and Google may process information outside the European Economic Area. Their privacy information is linked below. Google’s Terms of Service apply to reCAPTCHA.
privacy.contact.title: Email and telephone enquiries
privacy.contact.data: If you email or call us, we process your contact details and the information you provide to respond to your enquiry. An email may also include attachments and technical delivery information. Please send only information needed to deal with your request.
privacy.contact.basis: Where your enquiry concerns entering into or performing a contract with you, the legal basis is Article 6(1)(b) GDPR. For other support, feedback and business correspondence, it is our legitimate interest in responding to enquiries under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR. Where we must retain correspondence to comply with a legal obligation, the legal basis is Article 6(1)(c) GDPR.
privacy.contact.retention: We keep correspondence for as long as needed to handle your enquiry and meet applicable statutory retention obligations. The relevant criteria are whether the matter remains open and whether the correspondence must be retained as a business, tax or legal record.
privacy.contact.google: Our contact mailbox uses Google Workspace. Google processes message content, attachments and routing information to provide and secure the email service. Processing may take place outside the European Economic Area. Google's Cloud Data Processing Addendum includes Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers where required. You can contact us for information about the safeguards applicable to your data and how to obtain a copy.
privacy.contact.googleLink: Google Workspace's Cloud Data Processing Addendum
privacy.required.title: Whether you need to provide data
privacy.required.body: You do not need an account or registration to read the website. Technical connection data is necessary to deliver its pages. Joining the waitlist is voluntary; it requires an email address and at least one platform choice. Beta interest is optional. Contacting us is also voluntary, but without the information needed to understand and answer your enquiry, we may be unable to help.
privacy.decisions.title: Automated decisions
privacy.decisions.body: This website does not profile visitors or make solely automated decisions about you that produce legal or similarly significant effects.
privacy.rights.title: Your rights
privacy.rights.intro: Subject to the conditions of the GDPR, you have the following rights:
privacy.rights.access: Access to your personal data and information about its processing (Article 15).
privacy.rights.correction: Correction of inaccurate data and completion of incomplete data (Article 16).
privacy.rights.portability: Data portability where processing is based on consent or a contract and carried out by automated means (Article 20).
privacy.rights.contact: To exercise your rights, contact us using the details above. We may need information to verify your identity and locate the data concerned.
privacy.objection.title: Your right to object
privacy.objection.body: Where we process your personal data on the basis of legitimate interests under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, you may object at any time on grounds relating to your particular situation. We will then stop that processing unless we demonstrate compelling legitimate grounds that override your interests, rights and freedoms, or the processing is needed to establish, exercise or defend legal claims (Article 21 GDPR).
privacy.complaint.title: Complaints
privacy.complaint.body: You may lodge a complaint with a data-protection supervisory authority, particularly in the EU Member State where you live or work, or where you believe an infringement took place. The authority responsible for us is:
privacy.complaint.name: Landesbeauftragte für Datenschutz und Informationsfreiheit Nordrhein-Westfalen
privacy.changes.title: Changes to this notice
privacy.changes.body: We update this notice when the website or the processing it describes changes.
privacy.delivery.title: Downloads and app updates
privacy.delivery.macos: The macOS download control requests release information from this website. Direct macOS builds use signed DMG downloads and signed update artifacts. Builds with direct updates enabled check getsituate.com for update information automatically and when you request a check; downloading an update makes further file requests. These requests disclose connection and technical request data to our hosting infrastructure as described above, not your workspace content. We use this data to deliver releases and protect the delivery service under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR.
privacy.delivery.tracking: Artifact downloads and update requests do not use a download counter or tracking identifiers. If you allow website analytics, a click on the website’s download link is measured separately; this does not establish that the download completed or the app was installed. Update status, the last successful check and downloaded update files are stored on your device to manage updates.
privacy.delivery.apple: iOS installation and updates are managed by Apple, not by the direct macOS updater. Apple processes account, device and download information under its own privacy information. Store and operating-system diagnostics are separate from Situate's local diagnostics.
privacy.app.local.title: App workspaces and device storage
privacy.app.local.content: The app reads and writes the workspace locations you choose. They contain documents, tasks, conversations, attachments, drafts and version history. These files can contain personal information about you or other people. Using local workspace features does not itself upload this content to a Situate server. If you choose a location synchronized or backed up by your operating system or another service, that service can receive copies under your configuration and its own terms.
privacy.app.local.credentials: AI connection settings and encrypted credentials are stored on your device, separately from portable workspace content. The keys protecting those credentials use platform secure storage. The app also remembers workspace locations and access permissions. This credential protection does not encrypt every workspace file, conversation or diagnostic record. Copying a workspace does not transfer its stored credentials.
privacy.app.local.retention: Workspace data remains in the selected storage until deleted there. Earlier content can remain in version history, recovery data or backups after you edit or delete a current file. Removing a workspace from the app's list does not delete its files. Local app settings, credentials, update files and diagnostics are separate from workspace files. Uninstalling the app must not be assumed to erase all of these copies or data already sent to another service.
privacy.app.ai.title: Connecting to AI services
privacy.app.ai.setup: The app connects directly to the AI service you configure using your own account or credentials, rather than a Situate-operated AI service. Model discovery, browser or device sign-in, token exchange and refresh, and identity checks can contact that provider before you send a chat message. The provider can receive authentication and account information, authorization metadata, client identifiers and technical connection data.
privacy.app.ai.requests: AI requests can include your prompt, conversation context, attachments, referenced file content, tool definitions and results, model settings and authentication information. Summarizing conversation context and generating activity comments can make additional model requests. A request is not limited to the latest message you typed. Consider other people's privacy before sending their information; do not send sensitive information unless you have established that the service and your use of it are appropriate.
privacy.app.ai.providers: Connections include OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter and compatible endpoints you configure. The Codex connection uses OpenAI's ChatGPT backend, which is distinct from the OpenAI API. OpenRouter can forward requests to downstream model providers. A custom endpoint may be on your device, on your local network or on a remote server; an HTTP endpoint does not protect requests with HTTPS.
privacy.app.ai.transfers: The selected provider, account type, settings and endpoint determine processing locations, retention, deletion options, training use and any onward recipients. Processing may take place outside the European Economic Area. OpenAI API data controls must not be assumed to apply to ChatGPT connections. There is no blanket promise of EU-only processing, zero retention or no training for all connections. Review the information for your account and any downstream provider before connecting; deleting local content does not delete provider-held copies.
privacy.app.ai.openrouter: OpenRouter privacy policy and model-provider practices
privacy.app.tools.title: Remote content and app tools
privacy.app.tools.body: Displaying a remote image in a document can contact its host and disclose your IP address and technical request information. Opening external links contacts the linked service. Agent tools and shell commands can read or change files and contact additional services within the access available to them. Data sent by those actions is not limited to AI providers. Use only tools, plugins and endpoints you trust; access to them is not a guarantee of a filesystem or network sandbox.
privacy.app.diagnostics.title: Local app diagnostics
privacy.app.diagnostics.body: The app records local diagnostic events to help investigate faults. They include timestamps, operation results and pseudonymous workspace, device and session identifiers. These identifiers are not anonymous. Diagnostic storage is device-local and separate from workspace history, with a 256 MiB logical budget and 4 MiB segments; older segments are evicted as storage fills. This is not a days-based retention period.
privacy.app.diagnostics.sharing: The app does not automatically upload these diagnostics to Situate or use a Situate-operated usage analytics or crash-reporting collector. If you choose to send logs, screenshots, files or attachments for support, we receive the information you send and handle it as correspondence described below. Review it first and remove unrelated personal information and secrets. Apple or your operating system may process separate diagnostic reports according to your platform settings.
